name: Mansa Musa's Pilgrimage to Mecca
summary: Mansa Musa, ruler of the Mali Empire (the world's largest gold producer), makes his hajj to Mecca with a caravan of 60,000 men and 80-100 camels laden with gold. Distributing gold lavishly in Cairo, he single-handedly depresses gold prices in Egypt for over a decade. European cartographers (the Catalan Atlas, 1375) subsequently depict him on their maps, making West African wealth visible to Mediterranean audiences.

_quarry.structural_significance: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage demonstrates that major civilizations existed outside the European-Mediterranean axis that European cartographers were beginning to map; his gold distribution has measurable economic effects on Egyptian currency; the Mali Empire's wealth is the commercial prize that later motivates Portuguese exploration of the West African coast (1415-1488); this single pilgrimage puts Mali on the medieval world map literally and figuratively
